transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-12 17:00:00 UTC
Duration: 79 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Lukas Müller (Redwood Runtime), Jamie Ortiz (Redwood Product), Maria Gonzalez (Aurora CTO), Ben Yu (Aurora SRE), Ethan Park (ML Eng), Sana Iqbal (Platform)
---
Auto-summary (auto-generated, noisy): Discussed OpenTelemetry integration for per-token metrics, tradeoffs of sampling vs full tracing, prefix/KV cache hit instrumentation, dashboards for token-level cost attribution, on-prem collector and VPC network constraints. Agreed to share configs and run bench.
---
00:00 Speaker: Alex Chen: ok folks welcome, thanks for joining, um today's focused on the observability angle — opentel and token-level metrics on the redwood runtime. we wanted to show some concrete traces and dashboards and then dig into on-prem collector options and kv-cache telemetry.
02:12 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: thanks Alex. Maria here. we have a strict SLO for p95 latency and also need to attribute tokens to cost centers for billing, so token-level is must. also curious about network overhead of otel on our VPC.
04:01 Speaker: Priya Rao: yeah great point Maria. quick note: we usually recommend a hybrid sampling strategy — keep full traces for error/slow paths, and aggregate counters for steady-state token counts to avoid explosion. we'll show an example later.
06:20 Speaker: Ben Yu: hi all, Ben — SRE — basically we're worried about OTEL collector CPU on on-prem boxes. can you quantify collector overhead? and how does continuous batching change traces?
07:11 Speaker: Lukas Müller: sure ben, so there's two layers: instrumenting the runtime to emit spans and metrics, and the collector/transport. the runtime emits a lightweight per-request span and optional per-token events. the per-token stream can be configured: full events, sampled events, or summary counters. full per-token events are the heaviest option.
09:05 Speaker: Ethan Park: quick clar — when you say per-token events, is that one span per token or events inside a single span? we care because Jaeger storage can blow up.
09:45 Speaker: Priya Rao: good question. implementation is events inside a single request span — so tokens are emitted as event-type annotations on the ongoing stream, not separate top-level spans. that drastically reduces span-count explosion while keeping timing. but if you enable per-token spans for debug, yes you'll create many spans.
11:30 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: and these events include KV cache hit/miss tags? how granular can we go?
12:10 Speaker: Lukas Müller: we attach attributes to each token event: token_index, predicted_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit:true/false, batch_id, model_variant, quantization_profile. for privacy we don't send token text in production by default.
14:03 Speaker: Ben Yu: ok, that's useful. what's the overhead of adding kv_cache_hit attribute per token vs just a per-request counter of hits/misses?
15:22 Speaker: Priya Rao: per-token attributes let you correlate cache misses with token latency spikes and RTT. the cost is higher in collector throughput. recommended: enable per-token attributes for 1% sampling on production and full per-request counters always.
17:00 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: does redwood provide the otel collector config we can drop into our cluster? and do you support OTLP/gRPC, or just HTTP?
17:35 Speaker: Alex Chen: yes we have a reference otel-collector.yml and a Grafana dashboard JSON. we support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP. gRPC is preferred for throughput. we'll share the link after call.
19:20 Speaker: Ethan Park: you mentioned continuous batching earlier — how do batch boundaries show up in traces?
20:05 Speaker: Lukas Müller: batch boundaries are recorded as attributes: batch_size, batch_latency_ms, and we also emit a synthetic span for the batching window if you enable it. that helps visualize head-of-line waiting. in the trace you'll see request span start -> wait_for_batch span -> runtime compute span -> token events.
22:45 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: any recommended retention or sampling strategy for token-level traces? we have limited storage on-prem.
23:30 Speaker: Priya Rao: recommended pattern: 100% counters for tokens and cache stats, 1-5% of token-events sampled for traces for production, and 100% for errors/requests over p95. keep detailed token-event retention short (7 days) and aggregated counters longer (90 days).
25:10 Speaker: Ben Yu: on quantization — do you see different token decode latencies across int8 vs int4? any telemetry baked in to attribute slow tokens to quantization artifact?
26:05 Speaker: Lukas Müller: yes, we record model_execute_duration_ms per token batch and quantization_profile as an attribute. int4 tends to have slightly more variance in tail latencies; you can catch that by correlating quantization_profile with token_latency distribution.
28:00 Speaker: Ethan Park: is there a way to get token-level cost attribution in Grafana? per-route cost?
28:40 Speaker: Priya Rao: we emit token_count, token_cost_estimate (derived), and route labels. dashboard JSON includes a cost table by route/model/tenant. the token_cost_estimate is calculated server-side using your pricing rules or our default unit-cost.
30:12 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: curious about secure export — does OTEL exporter send metadata that would be considered PII? we need to avoid sending prompt content out of the VPC.
31:05 Speaker: Alex Chen: by default we strip token text before export; only hashes or token ids if you enable. for on-prem/private deploys you can configure collector to never egress traces outside VPC; we also support direct push to customer-managed datastores.
33:00 Speaker: Ben Yu: follow-up on network overhead — can batching reduce export traffic by aggregating events?
33:40 Speaker: Lukas Müller: yes, we batch telemetry events in the runtime and the otel-collector; you can tune batch_size and batch_timeout. telemetry batching reduces payloads but increases the chance of losing the very last events on sudden shutdown unless you enable reliable exporter.
35:50 Speaker: Sana Iqbal: for our compliance team, audit logs are a requirement. do traces and metrics feed into the same audit store?
36:30 Speaker: Jamie Ortiz: Audit logs are separate: we log control-plane events and token-level metrics are stored as metrics/trace artifacts. you can route traces to your audit store if needed, but typically metrics (token counts, cache hits) are the auditable aggregates.
38:05 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: if we run Redwood Private on-prem, would the otel-collector be managed by us or by Redwood? and what's the recommended topology?
38:45 Speaker: Priya Rao: for Private deployments we ship a reference collector you can run in your mesh; typically customers deploy one collector per cluster with an optional forwarder in a central monitoring VPC. for air-gapped customers we provide an offline config bundle.
40:20 Speaker: Ben Yu: can you show an example trace?
40:45 Speaker: Alex Chen: yes, switching to screen, here's a sample Jaeger trace from a reddwood runtime run — below the trace you can see wait_for_batch span, runtime_compute span and token events. [link: https://redwood.ai/slides/otel-deepdive.pdf] (note: transcript may misread url)
41:50 Speaker: Speaker 1: uh that link's useful, thanks.
42:30 Speaker: Priya Rao: reading trace: token event at t=120ms had kv_cache_hit=false and corresponding spike in token_latency_ms. downstream you can see a fetch_to_kv_store span that adds ~80ms.
44:15 Speaker: Ethan Park: what KV store are you typically integrating with in private deployments? redis? dynamo?
44:55 Speaker: Lukas Müller: we've integrated commonly with Redis, Memcached, and customer-managed RocksDB for on-disk. we ship adapters for common backends. the KV fetch span includes backend type and latency but redacts keys by default.
46:20 Speaker: Ben Yu: and if we want to debug a specific customer flow where cache misses spike, can we temporarily enable full token spans? what's the impact?
46:55 Speaker: Priya Rao: yes you can flip debug-mode per-route or per-tenant for a limited time window. expect collector throughput to increase by roughly 8-12x depending on token rates; storage blowup is significant so use short windows and offload to a temporary bucket.
48:30 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: for our finance team we need exported CSVs of token_count per route per day. is that available?
48:55 Speaker: Alex Chen: yes we have a scheduled export job that can push daily aggregates to S3 or to your object store. we can map route -> cost center labels beforehand.
50:12 Speaker: Sana Iqbal: what's the recommended dashboard to detect regression when you flip quantization profile in a canary?
50:45 Speaker: Jamie Ortiz: use the per-route token_latency_p95 over time, plus kv_cache_miss_rate and token_cost_estimate; our canary dashboard compares baseline vs canary side-by-side and flags percent regressions. we'll share the Grafana JSON.
52:05 Speaker: Ben Yu: any integrations with datadog/honeycomb for tracing or do we have to use OTEL only?
52:35 Speaker: Priya Rao: we export OTLP to any backend that supports it — Datadog, Honeycomb, Lightstep, Jaeger, Zipkin. for Honeycomb we recommend the Beeline conversion layer for best sampling.
54:10 Speaker: Ethan Park: edge case — what if we have a model fallback chain (fast small model then expensive large model)? how do traces handle fallback attribution?
55:00 Speaker: Lukas Müller: we instrument routing as part of the span: primary_model_attempt span and fallback_model_call spans, each with token counts and latency. that way costs are attributed to the actual executed model.
56:22 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: are instrumented metrics signed or tamper-evident for compliance? we need to detect modifications to audit metrics.
57:00 Speaker: Jamie Ortiz: we can enable write-once append-only logs for control-plane events; metric integrity is usually handled via secure storage and role-based access. we can discuss a hardened pipeline for mitm/tamper evidence if needed.
58:30 Speaker: Ben Yu: can you explain how continuous batching affects p50 vs p99 — it sounds like it helps throughput but hurts tail?
59:10 Speaker: Lukas Müller: correct: batching increases throughput and lowers average cost per token but introduces head-of-line latency for early requests waiting to fill a batch. our adaptive batching algorithm tries to balance by setting batch_timeout based on observed arrival rates. the trace shows wait_for_batch spikes as small gold vertical bars before compute.
61:05 Speaker: Ethan Park: is there SDK support for sampling rules to instruct the collector which traces to keep (e.g., keep all traces for tenant X)?
61:40 Speaker: Priya Rao: yes, collector config supports tenant-aware sampling rules and dynamic updates through the control plane; you can keep 100% for critical tenants and 1% for baseline.
63:00 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: how would we instrument model quantization switching — is it an attribute at the route or at the token level?
63:38 Speaker: Lukas Müller: quantization_profile is attached at both route and token-event level. route-level gives global context; token-level helps correlate per-token variance with quantization.
65:05 Speaker: Ben Yu: a practical ask — can you produce a small quickstart: otel-collector.yml + prom gateway config + grafana json that we can drop into our dev cluster?
65:35 Speaker: Alex Chen: yes — action: we'll drop quickstart bundle into the shared drive and ping you. expect a one-click Helm chart and a sample k8s manifest.
66:50 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: ok, let's outline the follow-ups: we want bench results for our on-prem instance, the otel config, and a live bench run.
67:30 Speaker: Alex Chen: agreed. Priya — Lukas — you'll lead the artifacts. Ben/Ethan — you'll provision the env. we'll schedule the live bench week of 2025-03-24.
68:55 Speaker: Speaker 2: mm-hmm sounds good.
69:30 Speaker: Priya Rao: just one more note on token-cost calculation: if you have multi-tenant routing, tag token events with tenant_id (hashed) so you can roll up cost per tenant without exposing prompt content.
71:10 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: great. thanks everyone. we'll expect the collector config and the dashboard.
72:00 Speaker: Alex Chen: thanks for the time. we'll follow up with the bundle and the bench plan.
73:15 Speaker: Ethan Park: thanks all, bye.
73:40 Speaker: Ben Yu: bye.
74:00 Speaker: Maria Gonzalez: bye.
